title: Affine compactness of the locally invertible open
statement: Let $W$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be finite locally free $\mathcal O_W$-modules with varying ranks [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], and let $\varphi:M\to N$. Let $U_\varphi$ be its locally invertible open [def-sc-module-map-iso-locus]. For every affine open $V\subseteq W$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the subset $V\cap U_\varphi$ of $W$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Final determinant sentence; Tag 05GD, Lemma 10.79.4(3), local matrix proof

proof.text: For each x in V, take finite free neighbourhoods for M and N using the proved source-library exists_mem_over_iso_free. Refine their intersection with V to an affine open U using exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset. Restrict the two frames to U via overIsoFreeEquiv, restrictCompIso and restrictFreeIso. This is the proved private helper exists_affine_compact_isoLocus_neighbourhood.

Apply the affine finite free principal-open identity to each such U. Its intersection with the isomorphism locus is a basic open, affine by IsAffineOpen.basicOpen and compact by IsAffineOpen.isCompact.

These U form an open cover of V. Use hV.isCompact.elim_finite_subcover to select finitely many. Each U lies in V, so a pointwise set-membership argument identifies V intersect the locus with the finite union of U intersect the locus. Finset.isCompact_biUnion proves compactness of that union.

QuasiCompact and quasiCompact_iff_forall_isAffineOpen supply the generic conversion, not compactness of the module-map locus.

No module-map iso-locus definition or vector-bundle universal locus theorem in Mathlib or the library.
